classification.difficultyReason: Requires complete geometrical proofs combining exterior angles, supplementary angles and triangle classification.

content.prompt: Show these properties, using full reasoning.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with A at lower left, B above, and C at lower right; AC extends through C to D. Interior angle ABC is 60 degrees and exterior angle BCD is 120 degrees.
spec.mathematics: A, C and D are collinear in that order. The labelled angles are ∠ABC = 60° and ∠BCD = 120°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied vertex labels, angle arcs and numerical givens are visible.

answer.short: $\angle BAC=60^{\circ}$ and $\angle BCA=60^{\circ}$. All three angles are $60^{\circ}$, so $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral.
answer.worked:
By the exterior angle theorem,
$$\begin{align*}
\angle BAC &= 120^{\circ}-60^{\circ}\\
\angle BAC &= 60^{\circ}.
\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$:
$$\begin{align*}
\angle BCA &= 180^{\circ}-120^{\circ}\\
\angle BCA &= 60^{\circ}.
\end{align*}$$
Together with $\angle ABC=60^{\circ}$, all three angles are equal. Sides opposite equal angles are equal, so $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral.

spec.description: Triangle PQR with P at lower left, R above P, and Q to the right. PQ extends through Q to S towards the upper right. Interior angle PRQ is 30 degrees and exterior angle RQS is 105 degrees.
spec.mathematics: P, Q and S are collinear in that order. The labelled angles are ∠PRQ = 30° and ∠RQS = 105°. Source-relative shape is retained; drawn angles are schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied vertex labels, angle arcs and numerical givens are visible.

answer.short: $\angle RPQ=\angle RQP=75^{\circ}$, so $PR=QR$ and $\triangle PQR$ is isosceles.
answer.worked:
By the exterior angle theorem,
$$\begin{align*}
\angle RPQ &= 105^{\circ}-30^{\circ}\\
\angle RPQ &= 75^{\circ}.
\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$:
$$\begin{align*}
\angle RQP &= 180^{\circ}-105^{\circ}\\
\angle RQP &= 75^{\circ}.
\end{align*}$$
Thus $\angle RPQ=\angle RQP$. Sides opposite equal angles are equal, so $QR=PR$ and $\triangle PQR$ is isosceles.
